subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU fitment, throughput targets & go/no-go logistics
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosys.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@heliosys.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Helio RFI follow-up: throughput targets and GPU preferences

Olga / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Procurement and infra are aligned on the high-level requirements, but we need a short, concrete table to take to our execs:

- Preferred GPU families (cost vs. tail-latency tradeoffs)
- Recommended reserved pool sizes for sustained 100 QPS and safe burst to 300 QPS
- Expected median & 95th percentile token latency for a 7B decoder LLM and a 70B decoder LLM under those pools

Can you also call out fallbacks (smaller quantized variants, region fallback) and whether you can guarantee isolation for our PCI-adjacent workloads?

We'd like that by Wednesday EOD PST so we can get internal sign-off.

—Samir
Procurement, Helio Systems
Attachment: helio-rfi-questions.pdf (listed)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosys.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helio RFI follow-up: throughput targets and GPU preferences

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a short workbook with the sizing scenarios (capacity_workbook_helio.xlsx) and a one-page appendix on isolation options. Key points up-front:

- GPU families we recommend: H100 for 70B-class models (best tail-latency at scale); A100-80GB for cost-balanced 13–30B workloads; L4 or A10G as cost-effective options for 7B-like models at high QPS.

- For sustained 100 QPS (mixed 7B/70B split 75/25): reserve plan = 8 H100-GPUs + 12 A100-equivalents (packed into 6 nodes) with autoscale buffer to add 4 A100s for burst to 300 QPS. Workbook shows slotting and token budgets.

- Latency expectations (approx, P95): 7B decoder: 60–120ms depending on batching; 70B decoder (H100): 180–300ms at P95. Median numbers are significantly lower (P50 ~ 30–70ms for 7B, ~90–140ms for 70B). The workbook includes measured runs from our test harness.

- Fallbacks: We support quantized 70B variants (int8) with ~1.3x latency improvement and small quality delta; automatic model variant routing is supported. Region fallback is supported but will change egress/network characteristics — we document expected delta in the workbook.

- Isolation: Dedicated pools provide tenant-level isolation, separate KV cache, and network ACLs. For PCI-adjacent workloads, we can enable Private deployment with customer VPC peering and KMS-backed key management — that option is in the appendix.

Next steps we propose:
1) We finalize the workbook numbers & sign the mutual action plan (MAP) — quick version attached.
2) If you want, we can run a short A/B load test using your canonical prompt set on a pilot pool (2 H100 + 4 A100 equiv) — take ~48 hours to provision and run.

Deliverables attached: Helio_RFI_Response_v3.pdf, capacity_workbook_helio.xlsx, deployment_playbook_snippet.txt

If Wednesday EOD PST is tight, we can extend to Thursday morning — what works?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Helio_RFI_Response_v3.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosys.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@heliosys.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helio RFI follow-up: throughput targets and GPU preferences

Olga —

This is great, thank you. Procurement is happy to see the isolation options. A couple of clarifying Qs before we take to execs:

1) Can you show cost delta for H100 vs A100 baseline at the 100 QPS sustained plan (spread per month)?
2) For the pilot A/B load test, will Redwood provide the pilot environment and monitoring (console + traces), or do we need to route samples to our monitoring?

We can do Thursday morning for the final workbook if that helps. Also: our Security team asks for the SOC2 report — can you attach or point to the audit artifact?

—Samir

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosys.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helio RFI follow-up: throughput targets and GPU preferences

Samir —

Short answers to your clarifying questions:

1) Cost delta: see tab "MonthlyCostBreakdown" in capacity_workbook_helio.xlsx — summary: H100 reserved pool adds ~35–45% monthly cost vs an A100-heavy mix for the same P95 SLAs because of H100 unit pricing, but it reduces tail latency and improves consistency for the 70B model. We included a blended-case where you keep most traffic on A100 and reserve a small H100 emergency pool — we call that "hybrid-fast-path".

2) Pilot provisioning & monitoring: Redwood will provision the pilot pool in the Dedicated environment (we handle capacity + model deploy). We will enable console access for your SREs (read-only by default), and we will stream traces/metrics to a temporary shared workspace we create. If you prefer to forward a subset of traces to your internal monitoring, we can set that up; most customers use both.

3) SOC2: attach: https://drive.redwood.internal/security/SOC2-Report-2026.pdf (read-only link included in the related_links). If you need an NDA'd copy, we can route through legal.

Proposed MAP milestone:
- Thu 11/12 morning: finalize workbook and sign MAP (DocuSign link above)
- Mon 11/16: provision pilot pool and run 48hr A/B (we'll share runbook)
- Mon 11/23: internal review + exec decision

If that cadence works, we'll prepare the MAP and the DocuSign envelope and loop in contracts.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_workbook_helio.xlsx (referred)
